content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Asynchronous and Semi-Synchronous Replication in MySQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"MySQL replication is a process that enables data from one MySQL database server (the source) to be copied automatically to one or more database servers (replicas). Choosing the right replication topology is crucial for balancing performance, availability, and data durability."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Asynchronous Replication"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In asynchronous replication, the source server writes events to its binary log (binlog) and commits transactions without waiting for confirmation from the replicas. The replicas retrieve the events from the source's binlog at their own pace and apply them locally."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"High Performance: The source does not experience network latency penalties from waiting for replica acknowledgments."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Risk of Data Loss: If the source crashes unexpectedly, transactions that have been committed on the source might not have reached the replicas yet, leading to potential data divergence upon failover."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Semi-Synchronous Replication"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Semi-synchronous replication introduces a safety check. When a client performs a transaction write on the source, the source waits after committing the transaction until at least one replica has received and logged the events to its relay log before returning a success status to the client."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Improved Durability: Guarantees that committed transactions exist on at least one replica, reducing the risk of data loss during a source crash."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Performance Trade-off: Transaction commit times are bounded by network round-trip latency to the replicas."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Semi-Synchronous Replication"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"To configure semi-synchronous replication, you must load the appropriate plugins on both the source and the replica instances."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"INSTALL PLUGIN rpl_semi_sync_source SONAME 'semisync_source.so';\nINSTALL PLUGIN rpl_semi_sync_replica SONAME 'semisync_replica.so';"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"After installing the plugins, you need to enable semi-synchronous replication dynamically using SQL commands or by modifying your configuration file (my.cnf)."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"SET GLOBAL rpl_semi_sync_source_enabled = ON;\nSET GLOBAL rpl_semi_sync_replica_enabled = ON;"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"If a semi-synchronous replica falls too far behind, MySQL can automatically fall back to asynchronous replication to prevent the source from hanging indefinitely. You can configure this timeout threshold as follows:"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"SET GLOBAL rpl_semi_sync_source_timeout = 10000;"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Asynchronous replication is ideal for scale-out read performance where occasional data loss on failover is acceptable. Semi-synchronous replication bridges the gap by providing enhanced data safety with a minor trade-off in write latency, making it a standard choice for high-availability database architectures."}]
